standard_prerequisites.name: The determinant of a two-term complex of finite projective modules as det(L^0) tensor det(L^{-1})^{tensor -1}
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the object the functor is built from.

standard_prerequisites.name: The three conditions on the maps of a good diagram established earlier in the section
standard_prerequisites.use: Are what make det(c^bullet) o det(b^bullet)^{-1} a sensible definition.

standard_prerequisites.name: The homotopic-surjections lemma comparing the determinants of two maps that agree up to homotopy
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives independence of det(a^bullet) from the chosen good diagram in the identity case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Representation of morphisms from a bounded complex of finite projective modules by homotopy classes of maps of complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the construction be carried out on good complexes rather than abstractly.

core_obligations: Call a two-term complex with finite projective terms in degrees -1 and 0 good, note that every object of the source category is represented by one, and use that morphisms between good complexes in the derived category are homotopy classes of maps of complexes to justify working with the determinant det(L^bullet) = det(L^0) tensor det(L^{-1})^{tensor -1} (proof lines 37150-37162).

Define a good diagram for a quasi-isomorphism a^bullet : L^bullet -> K^bullet as a commuting-up-to-homotopy triangle through a good M^bullet whose maps b^bullet and c^bullet satisfy the three earlier conditions, and define det(a^bullet) = det(c^bullet) o det(b^bullet)^{-1} (proof lines 37165-37182).

Prove existence of good diagrams: choose a surjection p : R^{oplus n} -> K^{-1}, form the good complex M^bullet with terms L^{-1} oplus R^{oplus n} and L^0 oplus R^{oplus n} and differential d oplus 1, and take b^bullet the projection and c^bullet given by a^{-1} oplus p in degree -1 and a^0 oplus d o p in degree 0, verifying the conditions (proof lines 37185-37200).
Prove independence over the identity: for a good diagram over id^bullet, use the homotopic-surjections lemma to get det(c^bullet) = det(b^bullet), hence det(id^bullet) = id (proof lines 37203-37213).

Analyse composition of quasi-isomorphisms and good diagrams, using the same diagrammatic machinery to establish well-definedness of det(a^bullet) in general and its compatibility with composition (proof lines 37216 and following to 37290).
Conclude that det is a functor on the stated categories and that the canonical elements delta(L) in det(L) are natural under isomorphisms, giving det(a)(delta(L)) = delta(K) (statement conclusion).
difficulty_reason: The lemma packages the determinant constructions of the surrounding section into a functor det from the category of perfect complexes with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] and isomorphisms as morphisms, to the category of invertible modules with isomorphisms as morphisms; it also asserts that a rank 0 perfect object L with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] carries a canonical element delta(L) in det(L) such that for every isomorphism a : L -> K in D(R) one has det(a)(delta(L)) = delta(K) (source lines 37123-37147). The proof is a substantial construction-and-verification. It first calls a two-term complex with finite projective terms good, notes that every object of the source category is represented by one, and that morphisms between good complexes in the derived category are homotopy classes of maps of complexes, so that the previously studied determinant det(L^bullet) = det(L^0) tensor det(L^{-1})^{tensor -1} can be used (proof lines 37150-37162). For a quasi-isomorphism a^bullet : L^bullet -> K^bullet it introduces the notion of a good diagram: a commuting-up-to-homotopy triangle through an auxiliary good complex M^bullet whose maps b^bullet and c^bullet satisfy the three conditions established earlier; det(a^bullet) is then defined as det(c^bullet) composed with det(b^bullet)^{-1}, and the proof must show that good diagrams always exist and that this definition does not depend on the diagram chosen (proof lines 37165-37182). Existence is constructive: choosing a surjection R^{oplus n} -> K^{-1}, the proof builds the good complex M^bullet = (L^{-1} oplus R^{oplus n}) -> (L^0 oplus R^{oplus n}) with the projection b^bullet and the map c^bullet using a^{-1} oplus p in degree -1 and a^0 oplus d o p in degree 0, and checks the conditions (proof lines 37185-37200). Independence for the identity is then immediate from the homotopic-surjections lemma, which gives det(c^bullet) = det(b^bullet) for a good diagram over the identity, so det(id^bullet) = id (proof lines 37203-37213). The proof continues by analysing composition of quasi-isomorphisms and good diagrams, and completes the independence, functoriality and the canonical element delta by the same diagrammatic machinery (rest of the counted proof span, source lines 37216-37290). The non-routine content is the existence construction for good diagrams, the use of the homotopic-surjections lemma to get independence over the identity, and the diagrammatic treatment of composition.
